Daily Courier Opinion

Why the council should fix the bridge first

By Jordan Ellis, columnist

The council has three projects on its list this year, and only enough money for two of them. The bridge on Mill Street carries more traffic than the other two projects combined, and the last inspection rated its deck as poor.

Fixing the bridge first is not the exciting choice. A new park would draw more attention at a ribbon cutting. But the cost of waiting grows every winter, because water gets into the cracks and the repair gets bigger.

The council should vote for the bridge at its meeting on Tuesday, and put the park on next year's list. That is the order a careful household would choose, and it is the order the town should choose too.
